title: Find the Longest Substring Containing Vowels in Even Counts
description:
Given the string `s`, return the size of the longest contiguous substring containing each vowel (`'a'`, `'e'`, `'i'`, `'o'`, `'u'`) an even number of times.

That is, inside the chosen substring, each of the five vowels `'a'`, `'e'`, `'i'`, `'o'`, and `'u'` must appear `0, 2, 4, ...` times. Consonants may appear any number of times. If no non-empty valid substring exists, return `0`.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters.
hints: You only care about the parity (even or odd) of each vowel's count, not the exact count.
Encode the parities of the 5 vowels as a 5-bit integer bitmask (32 possible states), toggling the corresponding bit whenever you see a vowel.
A substring (i, j] has even counts of all 5 vowels if and only if the prefix bitmask at j equals the prefix bitmask at i. Record the first index where each of the 32 masks appears.

examples.explanation: The longest valid substring is "leetminicowor" (length 13), containing two e's, two i's, two o's, zero a's, and zero u's.
The longest valid substring is "leetc" (length 5), containing two e's and zero of all other vowels.
The entire string "bcbcbc" (length 6) contains zero of every vowel, which is even for all five vowels.
